newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England, regulator to clarify roles-Davies.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England, regulator to clarify roles-Davies.

text.p: Britain's top financial watchdog the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) and the Bank of England are together deciding how to handle banking collapses under the government's new regulatory regime, the Financial Times said on Monday.

Howard Davies, deputy governor of the Bank and chairman designate of the SIB, told the FT the Treasury would probably publish a memorandum of understanding aimed at clearing up doubts about who would step in if a the event of a bank failure.

His comments follow industry uncertainty over the Bank's position as "lender of last resort" and the enlarged Super-SIB's responsibility for banking supervision, which it gained last month from the Bank.
"There will be value in explaining to the marketplace how all this works so people know when they think they are going bust, to whom they should address themselves," Davies told the FT.

While the chairman of a bank in trouble would be expected to first contact the SIB, the Bank -- which keeps its responsibility for the safety of the financial system under the new rules -- would become involved in any potentially serious failure, it added.

Davies also said the new system would eliminate possible conflicts, creating greater clarity about who was responsible for what. But the Bank and the SIB would have to forge a strong working relationship early on, he told the paper.

And the new SIB was likely to charge banks a direct fee to fund the costs of their supervision, something which would have to be balanced by a reduction in the contribution they currently make to the Bank, he said.
